comment: v2 script (voiceover/f1-v2-script.md). Per-line speaker; `after` = seconds of silence after the line (the last line's `after` becomes the section tail). Inline [pause s] markers add silence inside a line.

lines.speaker: bog
lines.text: Okay, quick question. [pause 0.3] Since when did everyone become an F1 fan?

lines.speaker: wec
lines.text: Since always! Look, I've got tickets!

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Well, not always. Today, Formula 1 feels like it's at the center of the universe. It's everywhere. Your friends watch it, it dominates your social media feeds, and the drivers are global cultural icons.

lines.speaker: bog
lines.text: Funny. I never got the memo.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Fair enough. Because rewind just fifteen years, and Formula 1 was a completely different world.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: The ultimate "old boys' club." A highly exclusive, Euro-centric billionaire's playground. You either grew up watching it... or you simply didn't care.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: So how did a sport wrapped in elitism and complex engineering suddenly become the most talked-about entertainment brand on the planet?

lines.speaker: wec
lines.text: Ooh. Good question.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Let's go and find out.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: To understand the boom, we have to talk about 2017. [pause 0.3] For decades, Formula 1 was run by Bernie Ecclestone.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Bernie was brilliant at making F1 rich. But his philosophy was all about exclusivity. The sport relied on expensive TV packages, luxury watch sponsors, and artificial scarcity.

lines.speaker: bog
lines.text: So the door was just... closed?

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Pretty much. Social media? Drivers were essentially banned from sharing behind-the-scenes footage in the paddock. The sport was aggressively keeping the modern world out.

lines.speaker: wec
lines.text: I can't see anything. Not even a little bit.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Then, Liberty Media bought Formula 1 for 8 billion dollars.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: They immediately realized something crucial. [pause 0.3] F1 had a massive branding problem. But it also possessed the greatest untold stories in sports.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: So Liberty stopped treating Formula 1 like a traditional racing series, and started treating it like a global media company. They completely tore down the digital walls.

lines.speaker: wec
lines.text: Wait, is that a phone? Drivers are allowed phones now?

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Encouraged, actually. On YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok.

lines.speaker: bog
lines.text: Whoa. I can see the garage from here.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: F1 went from a closed-door society to an always-on reality show.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: But the real rocket fuel was a little show you might have heard of. [pause 0.3] Drive to Survive.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Before 2019, if you were a new fan tuning into a race, you just saw twenty identical-looking cars driving in circles. You had to understand aerodynamics and tire degradation to enjoy it.

lines.speaker: bog
lines.text: Yeah. That was me. I counted twenty cars and zero reasons to care.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Then Netflix changed the formula. They focused entirely on the humans inside the machines.

lines.speaker: wec
lines.text: Now you've got ego, pressure, rivalries! It's basically a soap opera at three hundred kilometers an hour.

lines.speaker: bog
lines.text: Okay, but wait. Who am I supposed to root for?

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: That's exactly the point. Suddenly, you weren't watching cars. You were watching ambition, ego, massive pressure, and bitter rivalries. You learned what was at stake for the guy fighting for tenth place just to keep his job.

lines.speaker: bog
lines.text: Huh. Okay. Now I want to know how tenth place turns out.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Drive to Survive gave audiences a reason to care. People who had never watched a motorsport in their lives were suddenly canceling their Sunday plans to watch Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton battle it out.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: F1 realized that people don't connect with lap times. [pause 0.4] They connect with stories.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: That storytelling strategy completely rewired who watches Formula 1. In just a few years, the sport experienced one of the fastest demographic shifts in modern history.

lines.speaker: bog
lines.text: Let me guess. Engineering nerds, mostly.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Let's check.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: The average fan age plummeted from 36 to 32.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: And today, a massive 43 percent of all F1 fans are under 35.

lines.speaker: wec
lines.text: And they're not all here for the same reason. Some come for the drivers. Some for the strategy. Some just for the atmosphere. Everyone walks in through a different door.

lines.speaker: bog
lines.text: Huh. So it's not one kind of fan.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Not even close. The biggest shift? The female fanbase. Women now make up 42 percent of F1's global audience, driving a cultural evolution.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: F1 is no longer just about engine suppliers. It's embedded in fashion, lifestyle, and pop culture.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: We're seeing major beauty brands like Charlotte Tilbury and Elemis sponsoring the F1 Academy. The season launches have turned into massive stadium concerts.

lines.speaker: wec
lines.text: So it's not just about the cars. I did not see that coming.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Formula 1 isn't just a race weekend anymore. [pause 0.4] It's a lifestyle that Gen Z wants to be a part of.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: And we can't ignore the United States. [pause 0.3] For decades, F1 tried and failed to crack the American market.

lines.speaker: bog
lines.text: So what changed?

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Fast forward to today, and the US hosts three of the most glamorous races on the calendar. Austin, Miami, and Vegas.

lines.speaker: wec
lines.text: Road trip! I'll drive. Well, someone's driving.

lines.speaker: bog
lines.text: I'll bring snacks.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Big tech has noticed, too. Apple recently secured a massive 150-million-dollar-a-year deal to broadcast F1 in the US.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: And Brad Pitt's mega-budget F1 movie dominated the global box office.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: The sport has saturated every layer of media.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Fifteen years ago, Formula 1 survived by locking its doors and asking you to pay for a glimpse inside.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: Today, it's booming because it threw the doors wide open.

lines.speaker: bog
lines.text: So... when's the next race?

lines.speaker: wec
lines.text: Already got the tickets.

lines.speaker: bog
lines.text: Wait, you only have two.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: I'll watch from the front row. Apparently everyone gets one now.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: By focusing on the people beneath the helmets and embracing the digital age, F1 stopped being just a race. It became the greatest traveling circus on Earth.

lines.speaker: mog
lines.text: And now, everyone has a front-row seat.
